A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoRAG research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original CoRAG evaluations on multi-hop QA and KILT, with decoding, ablation, robustness and supplementary results.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds teacher-model, retrieval-recall, fine-tuning-control and Qwen3 experiments.

M1.justification: The retrieval-chain procedure, training objectives, decoding strategies and early-stopping variant are retained. GPT-4o and Qwen3 experiments apply the existing framework; reciprocal rank fusion is introduced for recall evaluation, not the answer-generation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four multi-hop QA datasets, English Wikipedia corpus and KILT tasks. The added analyses reuse existing coverage without introducing new domains, populations or input scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 9 adds fine-tuned Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B with E5-large as matched baselines. Figure 7 adds un-fine-tuned Llama retrieval-chain scaling for comparison. The comparator sets in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged; AQA and Search-R1 are added only as citations.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce answer-match Recall@10/20/100 with reciprocal rank fusion, GPT-4o-generated training chains, Qwen3 backbones and a no-fine-tuning control. Existing experiments retain their stated settings. Newly disclosed dataset sample counts do not establish changed splits.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: a stronger-teacher ablation tests training-chain quality, Table 4 directly tests retrieval recall, Figure 7 isolates scaling without fine-tuning, and Table 9 tests transfer across model families. Earlier robustness, sampling, temperature and early-stopping analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Appendix C states that 95% bootstrap confidence intervals were computed for Tables 1–2 and reports statistical significance. v2 has no equivalent analysis. v3 supplies neither interval values nor resampling details and does not document additional independent runs.

E6.justification: Substantial new results cover teacher quality, retrieval recall, untuned scaling and Qwen3. For example, Table 4 reports MuSiQue Recall@20 of 54.6 for CoRAG versus 36.5 for E5-large; Table 9 reports 2WikiQA EM of 70.0 versus 52.1 for CoRAG-Qwen3-8B and its fine-tuned baseline. These are added comparisons; retained benchmark and appendix scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The chain formalization, likelihood-based selection, training losses and Pareto-fit mathematics are unchanged. Neither version presents theoretical proofs, and the added standard recall evaluation introduces no new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and claims about retrieval-chain training, test-time scaling and benchmark performance. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations linking teacher-chain quality to performance, fine-tuning to the scaling ceiling, and Qwen3 results to cross-family applicability. Section 7 explicitly limits the evidence to short-answer tasks, while Section 4.1 explains why HotpotQA and MuSiQue leaderboard settings are not directly comparable.

D1.justification: New Table 6 discloses per-dataset training and validation counts. The introduction expands the resource-availability statement from code to code, data and trained models. Existing hyperparameters, hardware information and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to AQA, Search-R1 and Qwen3. Related work distinguishes AQA's single-hop focus and Search-R1's reinforcement-learning approach, while retaining the paper's overall positioning around explicit fine-tuning and test-time scaling.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order are retained. Local edits clarify Current State and Next Action and update affiliation and venue information. New analysis, limitations, statistical-significance and checklist sections are inserted; the unchanged prompts move from Appendix C to D.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 4, 6 and 9 and Figure 7, expands Table 3, and gives the opening illustration a unified numbered caption. Existing graphics are reused, with table relocations, renumbering and page reflow rather than a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The retrieval-recall study, no-fine-tuning control and Qwen3 comparisons strengthen empirical support, while dataset counts and explicit applicability limits improve transparency. This provides a modest net improvement. The new statistical reporting remains incomplete: Appendix C omits interval values and bootstrap details, and its broad significance statement does not explain Table 2's retained FEVER exception.
